description_summary: Hourly near-surface analyses on the 2.5 km CONUS Western Expansion grid, from 2017-05-02 onward. This virtual dataset references NOAA's GRIB files and is optimized for spatial (map) access. It contains 13 analysis fields, with dimensions time, y, and x on the native Lambert Conformal Conic projection. Precipitation is not included.
description_details:
This dataset is available in the staging catalog. For the dynamical-catalog
example, set `DYNAMICAL_STAC_CATALOG_URL=https://stac-staging.dynamical.org/catalog.json`
before starting Python. The pystac example selects the staging catalog directly.

### Construction

Hourly RTMA analyses are represented as virtual references to NOAA's CONUS
Western Expansion GRIB files, on their native 2345 by 1597 Lambert Conformal
Conic grid. Each chunk contains one complete field at one analysis time.
The 13 fields include temperature, dew point, specific humidity, surface pressure,
terrain height, wind, cloud cover, ceiling, and visibility. Precipitation is not included.

Wind components are grid-relative; wind direction is relative to true north.
Ceiling and visibility retain the source's finite values. Consult the validation
report for their interpretation and historical limitations.

### Source

Source files are provided by [NOAA Open Data Dissemination](https://www.noaa.gov/information-technology/open-data-dissemination)
in the public [NOAA RTMA archive](https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-rtma/).

### Data availability

The archive begins at 2017-05-02 00:00 UTC and updates hourly. Missing source
files remain gaps. See the [draft validation report](https://dataset-validation-reports.dynamical.org/noaa-rtma-analysis-virtual/drafts/v0.1.0_2026-10-20T16-16/validation_report.html) for checked
coverage, source-archive gaps, and the ceiling/visibility findings.

### Storage

Storage for this dataset is generously provided by [AWS Open Data](https://aws.amazon.com/opendata/).

### Chunks

This dataset is stored in [Zarr](https://zarr.dev/) format, which splits each variable into a grid of **chunks** — the smallest unit read from storage. When possible, aligning your reads with this dataset's chunk grid can significantly improve data access speed.

The element count and coordinate span of this dataset:

| dimension | chunk |
|---|---|
| time | 1 (1 hour) |
| y | 1597 (4055.91 km) |
| x | 2345 (5955.6 km) |
| **uncompressed** | 28.6 MiB |

### Validation report

Review the [validation report](https://dataset-validation-reports.dynamical.org/noaa-rtma-analysis-virtual/drafts/v0.1.0_2026-10-20T16-16/validation_report.html) for variable availability, missing data, known quirks, fill values, value distributions, and sample plots.

This report is a draft awaiting acceptance. It has not been published as a stable validation report.
description_model: The Real-Time Mesoscale Analysis (RTMA) is NOAA NCEP's hourly analysis of near-surface weather conditions. It combines observations with a model background using two-dimensional variational assimilation.

variants.label: pystac
variants.code:
import icechunk
import pystac
import xarray as xr

catalog = pystac.Catalog.from_file("https://stac-staging.dynamical.org/catalog.json")
collection = catalog.get_child("noaa-rtma-analysis-virtual")
asset = collection.assets["icechunk-https"]

authorize = icechunk.containers_credentials({"s3://noaa-rtma-pds/": icechunk.s3_anonymous_credentials()})
repo = icechunk.Repository.open(
    icechunk.http_storage(asset.href),
    authorize_virtual_chunk_access=authorize,
)
session = repo.readonly_session("main")

ds = xr.open_zarr(session.store, chunks=None)
ds["temperature_2m"].sel(time="2025-01-01T00")
